title: Air India Modifying Dreamliners After FAA Issues Safety Directive Over Door Handle Defect
excerpt: The directive covers Boeing 787 models worldwide after reports of door assist handles detaching during pre-flight checks.
body:
• The FAA has issued an airworthiness directive for certain Boeing 787-8, 787-9 and 787-10 aircraft after door assist handles were found pulling loose during pre-flight checks
  • Air India, which operates 33 Boeing 787 Dreamliners, is modifying affected aircraft to install new retainer parts
  • The defect could cause injuries during emergencies and limit exit from the aircraft during time-limited evacuations
  • The directive takes effect on August 6 and applies to Dreamliner operators worldwide, including IndiGo's five leased 787s

Air India has begun modifying certain Boeing 787 Dreamliners in its fleet after the US Federal Aviation Administration issued a new airworthiness directive addressing a door handle defect that could compromise passenger safety during emergency evacuations.

What the FAA Found

"The directive covers certain Boeing 787-8, 787-9 and 787-10 models — the three variants of the aircraft commonly known as the Dreamliner."

The directive, which takes effect August 6, was prompted by reports of door assist handles becoming detached from their lower attach point in the doorway support bracket during pre-flight checks. The FAA said the defect could cause injuries to passengers, crew or maintenance personnel when opening doors, and could limit exit from the aircraft during time-limited emergency evacuations.

The directive covers certain Boeing 787-8, 787-9 and 787-10 models — the three variants of the aircraft commonly known as the Dreamliner. It requires operators to install a new retainer above the lower keyway of the support bracket assembly and either install a placard or mark the affected part. Some aircraft also require inspection of forward and aft door assist handles with applicable follow-up actions.

Air India's Fleet Exposure

Air India currently operates 33 Boeing 787 Dreamliners — 26 legacy 787-8 aircraft and seven 787-9s, including six that came from Vistara when the two airlines merged. The Dreamliners serve as the backbone of Air India's long-haul operations, connecting major Indian cities with destinations across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.

IndiGo, India's largest carrier, also operates five Dreamliners leased from Norwegian carrier Norse Atlantic, though the specific applicability of the directive to its fleet would depend on the aircraft's manufacturing details.

Context for Travellers

The directive is a compliance requirement rather than an immediate grounding order. Airlines are given a defined window to complete the modifications while continuing normal operations. For passengers on Air India's US-India routes — among the busiest long-haul corridors for the Indian diaspora — the modifications are expected to be completed during scheduled maintenance without affecting flight schedules.

The door handle issue adds to a series of safety-related directives Boeing has faced for the 787 programme in recent years, including earlier orders addressing water leak risks near electronic equipment bays and decompression panel inspections. Boeing has maintained that none of these issues pose an immediate flight safety threat and has worked with the FAA on corrective actions.
nri_angle: Air India's large Dreamliner fleet serving key US-India routes is affected by the directive, relevant to NRI travellers
